aggressive_definition_excerpt: Odds ratios differed little when cases were stratified by stage of disease at diagnosis or by histopathological grade.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: This population-based, case-control study in King County, Washington examined supplement use in 697 incident prostate cancer cases (ages 40-64) identified from the Puget Sound Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results program registry and 666 controls recruited from the same overall population using random-digit dialing sampling.
reason: The study analyzed incident prostate cancer overall. Although cases were stratified by stage and histopathological grade, the abstract does not identify an explicit advanced, high-grade, aggressive, metastatic, or lethal incident stratum.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Adjusted odds ratios (95% confidence limits) for the contrast of > or =7/week versus no use were as follows: multivitamins, 0.96 (0.73, 1.26); vitamin A, 0.59 (0.32, 1.06); vitamin C, 0.77 (0.57, 1.04); vitamin E, 0.76 (0.54, 1.08); calcium, 1.04 (0.61, 1.78); iron, 0.50 (0.13, 1.76); and zinc, 0.55 (0.30, 1.00).
estimate_classifications.reason: The vitamin E estimate pertains to overall incident prostate cancer, not an explicitly aggressive endpoint.
